standard.title: Draw conclusions
standard.description: draw conclusions in response to questions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have answered questions from personal experience. No formal prior HASS inquiry skills curriculum.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students draw conclusions in response to inquiry questions about their family, celebrations, places and ways of caring for places.

nodes.label: Using evidence to answer questions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use information from a source (story, photograph, observation) to answer an inquiry question, rather than relying on personal memory alone.
nodes.minimum_width: Answer one inquiry question using at least one piece of evidence from a provided source.
nodes.typical_width: Use information from multiple sources (photographs, observations, stories) to answer inquiry questions about family, places and celebrations; explain where the answer came from.
wider: Compare answers to the same question from different sources and discuss which source they find more useful and why
Identify when a source answers the question fully and when they need more information
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who treat all answers as opinions rather than evidence-based conclusions cannot draw conclusions in the next node — evidence-based reasoning is the prerequisite for conclusion-drawing.

response_modes.reason: Make the evidence-to-conclusion chain explicit: 'I know this because I saw/heard/read...' Use sentence stems and model the reasoning aloud before expecting students to do it independently.

success_criteria: Answers an inquiry question using at least one piece of evidence from a source
Can identify where the answer came from ('I know this because...')

nodes.label: Drawing conclusions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can draw a conclusion in response to an inquiry question about family, celebrations, places or caring for places, supported by evidence from sources.
nodes.minimum_width: Draw one conclusion in response to a provided inquiry question, supported by at least one piece of evidence.
nodes.typical_width: Draw conclusions about main people in family, important celebrations, features of special places, and ways of caring for places; support each conclusion with evidence from sources or observations.
wider: Draw conclusions about a place and suggest what would change if it were not cared for
Draw conclusions about why a celebration is important by comparing it across two different families or cultural groups

response_modes.reason: Conclusion-drawing integrates questioning, sourcing and evidence-use — model the full inquiry cycle explicitly before expecting students to execute it independently.

success_criteria: Draws at least one conclusion in response to an inquiry question
Supports the conclusion with at least one piece of evidence
